title: The polynomial ring over a Noetherian N-2 domain is N-2
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] integral domain which is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], and let $R[x]$ be the polynomial ring in one variable $x$ over $R$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] (an integral domain). Then $R[x]$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $L$ of the fraction field $K(x)$ of $R[x]$, the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), second assertion

proof.text: *Reduction to $R$ normal.* Let $K$ be the fraction field of $R$ and $R'\subseteq K$ the integral closure of $R$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Taking $L=K$ in the definition of N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], $R'$ is a finitely generated $R$-module, say by $r_1,\dots,r_m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] (with $L=K$) $R'$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] it is Noetherian. (a) $R'$ is N-2: let $L/K$ be finite. The integral closure of $R'$ in $L$ contains that of $R$ (as $R\subseteq R'$); conversely if $y\in L$ is integral over $R'$, then $R'[y]$ is integral over $R'$ (it lies in the integral closure of $R'$ in $L$, a subring [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]) and $R'$ is integral over $R$, so $y$ is integral over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive]. Hence both closures are the same ring $S$, finitely generated over $R$ by hypothesis, so over $R'\supseteq R$ by the same generators. (b) It suffices to prove that $R'[x]$ is N-2: the ring $R'[x]$ is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module (generated by $r_1,\dots,r_m$, comparing coefficients), hence integral over $R[x]$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; as $R\subseteq R'\subseteq K$, both $R[x]$ and $R'[x]$ lie in $K[x]$ and have the fraction field $K(x)$. For a finite extension $L/K(x)$, the argument of (a) with [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] shows that the integral closures of $R[x]$ and of $R'[x]$ in $L$ coincide; if this ring is a finitely generated $R'[x]$-module, it is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra]. So we replace $R$ by $R'$ and assume from now on that $R$ is a Noetherian normal N-2 domain. (This is the N-2 case of the finite-extension lemma used by the source, written out for the finite extension $R[x]\subseteq R'[x]$, whose fraction fields agree.)

proof.text: *Properties of $R[x]$.* The ring $R[x]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (it is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $R$, with $n=1$, $\mathfrak a=0$), an integral domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain], and a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] since $R$ is normal. Its fraction field is $K(x)$, the field of fractions of $K[x]$ [def-weil-rational-function-field] (every element of $K[x]$ is $f/c$ with $f\in R[x]$, $c\in R\setminus\{0\}$), which has the same characteristic as $K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), proof of the second assertion, second paragraph ('The ring R'[x] is normal', 'As R[x] is Noetherian')

proof.text: *Characteristic zero.* Suppose $K$ has characteristic $0$ and let $L/K(x)$ be a finite extension. By [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] $L$ is separable over $K(x)$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]; applied to the finitely generated subextension $K'=L$, whose transcendence basis over $K(x)$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] is empty because $L/K(x)$ is algebraic, this says that $L/K(x)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. By Step 2, $R[x]$ is a Noetherian normal domain with fraction field $K(x)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] shows that the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module. So $R[x]$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), proof of the second assertion, 'In characteristic zero we are done by Lemma lemma-domain-char-zero-N-1-2' (Tag 032M, whose proof is Lemma 032L plus separability in characteristic zero)

proof.text: *Characteristic $p$: reduction to purely inseparable extensions.* Suppose $K$ has characteristic $p>0$. By Step 2, $R[x]$ is a Noetherian domain whose fraction field $K(x)$ has characteristic $p$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-n2-char-p-purely-inseparable-criterion] it suffices to show: for every finite purely inseparable extension $L/K(x)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module. Fix such an $L$ for Steps 5 to 8.

*The field $L'(x^{1/q})$ containing $L$ (the details the source omits).* Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so $K\subseteq K(x)\subseteq L\subseteq\Omega$. Let $y_1,\dots,y_n$ be a $K(x)$-basis of $L$; by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] there are $e_i$ with $y_i^{p^{e_i}}\in K(x)$; put $q=p^e$, $e=\max_ie_i$, so $y_i^q=(y_i^{p^{e_i}})^{p^{e-e_i}}\in K(x)$. Write $y_i^q=f_i(x)/g_i(x)$ with $f_i,g_i\in K[x]$, $g_i

Since $\Omega$ is algebraically closed, choose $t\in\Omega$ with $t^q=x$ and, for every coefficient $a$ of every $f_i$ and $g_i$, an element $a^{1/q}\in\Omega$ with $(a^{1/q})^q=a$; let $c_1,\dots,c_m$ be these roots and $L'=K[c_1,\dots,c_m]\subseteq\Omega$. *$L'/K$ is finite purely inseparable:* as $c_j^q\in K$, the $K$-module $K[c_1,\dots,c_m]$ is spanned by the finitely many monomials $c^a$ with $0\le a_j<q$, so it is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra contained in a field, hence an integral domain finite over $K$, hence a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is an injective $K$-linear endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space, so surjective); and every $\alpha=\sum\lambda_ac^a\in L'$ ($\lambda_a\in K$) has $\alpha^q=\varphi(\alpha)=\sum\lambda_a^q(c^q)^a\in K$. *$L\subseteq L'(t)$:* for $f=\sum_ja_jx^j$ among the $f_i,g_i$ put $f^

proof.text: *Reduction to $L'(t)$.* Let $C$ be the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L'(t)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Since $L\subseteq L'(t)$ (Step 5), the integral closure of $R[x]$ in $L$ is $C\cap L$, an $R[x]$-submodule of $C$. As $R[x]$ is Noetherian (Step 2), [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] shows that it suffices to prove that $C$ is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), proof of the second assertion, 'As R[x] is Noetherian it suffices to show that the integral closure of R[x] in L'(x^{1/q}) is finite over R[x]'

proof.text: *$C=A[t]$, where $A$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $L'$.* (i) $t$ is transcendental over $L'$: otherwise $L'[t]$ is finite over $L'$, hence over $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] (Step 5: $L'/K$ finite), and $x=t^q\in L'[t]$ would satisfy a nonzero polynomial over $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-element], whereas the powers $1,x,x^2,\dots$ are $K$-linearly independent in $K[x]\subseteq K(x)$. So $L'[t]\subseteq\Omega$ is a polynomial ring in $t$ over $L'$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $L'(t)$ is its fraction field, and $A[t]\subseteq L'[t]$ is the polynomial ring over $A$. (ii) By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] (for $R$ and the finite extension $L'/K$) $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $L'$; so $A[t]$ is a normal domain [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] with fraction field $L'(t)$ (an element of $L'[t]$ is $h/c$ with $h\in A[t]$, $c\in A\setminus\{0\}$, clearing the denominators of its finitely many coefficients). (iii) $A[t]\subseteq C$: every element of $A$ is integral over $R\subseteq R[x]$, and $t$ is a root of the monic polynomial $T^q-x$ over $R[x]$; since $C$ is a subring of $L'(t)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] containing $A$ and $t$, it contains $A[t]$. (iv) $C\subseteq A[t]$: an element $z\in C$ satisfies a monic equation with coefficients in $R[x]\subseteq A[t]$, and lies in $L'(t)=\operatorname{Frac}(A[t])$, so $z\in A[t]$ by normality of $A[t]$ (ii).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032O (lemma-polynomial-ring-N-2, line 45411), proof of the second assertion, 'And this integral closure is equal to R'[x^{1/q}] with R subset R' subset L' the integral closure of R in L''

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Since $L'/K$ is a finite extension (Step 5) and $R$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], $A$ is generated as an $R$-module by finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_m$. Every element of $A[t]$ is $\sum_kb_kt^k$ with $b_k\in A$; writing $k=qs+r$ with $0\le r<q$ and $t^{qs}=x^s$, it is an $R[x]$-linear combination of the $qm$ elements $a_jt^r$ ($1\le j\le m$, $0\le r<q$). So $C=A[t]$ (Step 7) is a finitely generated $R[x]$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; by Steps 6 and 4 the integral closure of $R[x]$ in every finite purely inseparable extension of $K(x)$ is finite over $R[x]$, and $R[x]$ is N-2. Together with Steps 1 and 3 this proves the lemma.
